clue.text: Boatman elevated above Russian authority in report on market

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down clue, raising a word turns it bottom to top

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor, so a man of boats

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the Russian ruler's title is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tsar was the Russian emperor

explanation.surface: A setter climbs above a Russian official in an account of trading at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: TSAR is said 'zar', so ZAAR is a spelling of that sound; the setter Boatman is playfully the able seaman here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is an oriental marketplace, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 18
See 24
How crimes are committed: special agent in series of pictures

parts.note: a criminal's modus operandi, abbreviated MO, is his method

indicators.note: special suggests these letters are given an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A spy-novel aside on criminal methods, with a special agent appearing in a film sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is modus operandi, a criminal's method; 'special' is the anagram signal, and 'in' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A montage is a composite of images or film shots arranged in sequence.

clue.text: Weapons of choice for 24 16 3 and not their first, stolen from bombed arsenals

indicators.note: stolen from says some letters are taken away from the scrambled pool
bombed means blown apart, so the letters of arsenals are scattered
their first refers back to the words and and not, taking each one's opening letter

explanation.surface: A Bond villain's favoured arms, pilfered from wrecked arsenals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their first' gives A and N; 'stolen from bombed arsenals' removes them from a jumble of ARSENALS, leaving the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldfinger famously threatens Bond with an industrial laser beam in the film.

clue.text: Implacable Bond, with one outer failing on the surface

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the pooled letters fall into a new order, with the word on dropping out

parts.note: the article a stands for one
the word on, taken at face value as it sits on the clue's surface, is the part that drops out

explanation.surface: An unyielding Bond with one external part of him failing outwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool BOND, A and OUTER; the answer plus ON makes those letters. Boatman himself intended BOND as B on D, inside a scramble of A plus OUTER, with 'on the surface' holding it, a reading many solvers found loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unmoved, a close synonym of unappeasable.

clue.text: Female character of enduring quality?

parts.note: split as Fe and male: the chemical symbol for iron, then a word for a man, so a man of Fe

explanation.surface: A literary heroine whose personality has staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: a male of iron, i.e. Fe male, gives the clue word 'Female'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person called a figure of steel or toughness has unbreakable resolve and endurance.

clue.text: Smears Bond's car, apparently hiding gold

indicators.note: hiding says the car's letters conceal another piece within them

parts.note: the Aston Martin DBS was a Bond car
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Bond's car is daubed, apparently concealing bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' is a link: the gold sits inside the car's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear paint or a sticky substance on carelessly.

clue.text: Connery etc in 16 3: a media scandal, correct?

parts.note: Sean Connery and the other actors in Goldfinger make up its cast
the i is a British newspaper, one medium among the media
-gate, as in Watergate, names a scandal

explanation.surface: Was the Goldfinger cast caught in a press scandal?
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a UK daily paper, so 'a media' gives I; the question mark flags that sense of correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke severely, correcting someone by punishment or reproof.

clue.text: Find fault in code of foreign spy's gadget

parts.note: de is French for of
a bug is a hidden listening device

explanation.surface: Locating the flaw in a foreign spy's device by its code.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers remove errors from software by tracking and fixing faults, the verb's usual sense.

clue.text: Who broke Oddjob?

indicators.note: odd here means the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A question about who smashed Goldfinger's henchman Oddjob.
explanation.walkthrough: The henchman's name splits as 'Odd' plus 'job'.
explanation.definitionFit: Work and job are synonyms for employment or a task.

clue.text: One sells Soviet paintings to the West

indicators.note: westward in an across clue is right to left, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: red was the colour of Soviet communism
art means paintings

explanation.surface: A dealer smuggles Soviet artworks to the West.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is a merchant, someone whose business is selling goods.

clue.text: Factions blowing up agent receive a reward in full

indicators.note: blowing means squandering, losing the word up from the factions

parts.note: groups are factions

indicators.note: receive says the agent takes in a letter

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Rival factions blow up an agent and collect their bounty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' looks like an explosion, but 'blowing' means squandering, so the word 'up' is lost; 'receive' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross pay is earnings before any deductions, the full remuneration.

clue.text: Pussy Galore's first in movement to erase holy water source

indicators.note: movement says the letters are shifted about
first takes the opening letter of each part of the Bond girl's name

explanation.surface: Pussy Galore leads a campaign to abolish holy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives P and G; 'movement' mixes them with ERASE. Pussy Galore is the Bond girl of Goldfinger.
explanation.definitionFit: An asperge is a sprinkler used by priests to scatter consecrated water.

clue.text: Evil genius captures one confident of success

indicators.note: captures says the jumbled word holds another piece
evil means corrupted, so the letters of genius are twisted

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A Bond villain seizes someone sure of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil genius' reads as Goldfinger, the theme villain, but 'Evil' is the anagram signal and 'captures' the container signal; 'one' is AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine describes a cheerful optimism about outcomes.

clue.text: See 24
Stripped for king — was lustful as cover?

indicators.note: as cover says the sinful word wraps round the letter

parts.note: lust is a deadly sin, so being lustful is one way to have sinned
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king was undressed: was desire to blame?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that lust is only one example of sinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinned means having had the outer layer peeled off, as stripped does.

clue.text: Evil genius talking up exit, with doomed Connery obit in doubt

indicators.note: in doubt means unsettled, so all these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain hastens Bond's exit, with an obituary for the doomed Connery uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: This is Goldfinger's famous line to Bond over the laser in the 1964 film.
explanation.definitionFit: The quote is what Goldfinger, the scheming mastermind villain, says to Bond.

clue.text: See 18
Provide base, where entry of new leader would provide emphasis

indicators.note: the answer is what remains before a letter enters, so the letter is removed here

parts.note: to underline is to emphasise

indicators.note: leader is the opening letter of the word new

explanation.surface: Building a foundation, where a new leader would add weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding N (new leader) gives UNDERLINE, to emphasise; so the answer is that word without the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To underlie is to lie beneath something as its foundation.

clue.text: It's not right to pry into perverse sex lives

indicators.note: to pry into means to poke inside, putting the second piece within the first
perverse means twisted, so the letters of sex are reordered
not right means wrong or disordered, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Prying into people's twisted sex lives is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' turns ITS into IST, which goes into EXS from 'perverse sex'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live or be alive, so third-person singular forms match.

clue.text: Free thinker on perverse activity embraced by Bond girl in 16 3

indicators.note: embraced by says the girl's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Jill Masterson is the gold-painted Bond girl in Goldfinger
SM, sadomasochism, is a kinky practice

explanation.surface: A freethinker gets kinky with a Bond girl from Goldfinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' nods to his essay On Liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was a Victorian liberal philosopher who championed liberty of thought.

clue.text: Oddjob: without hesitation, a rat-like creature

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, the jumbled letters going round
odd means strange, so the letters of job are reordered

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Goldfinger's henchman Oddjob unhesitatingly becomes a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: The henchman's name splits as 'Odd' and 'job': JBO round ER, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerboa is a jumping desert rodent resembling a small rat.

clue.text: One wants to find good inside Mr Solo

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the solitary figure

parts.note: a loner goes solo, playfully titled Mr

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to find goodness inside Napoleon Solo, the TV spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Solo suggests the spy of The Man from U.N.C.L.E., but is just a solitary man.
explanation.definitionFit: A longer is a person who yearns or desires something, so wants it.

clue.text: Find courage, with girl in distress caused by evil genius

indicators.note: in distress suggests upheaval, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A girl in peril, menaced by a villain, must summon her nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers all fifteen letters of the opening words and 'girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the gold-obsessed master criminal villain of Fleming's novel and the 1964 film.

clue.text: Wave hits Bond's head in submerged vessel for future generations

indicators.note: in places the wave and letter within the other piece

parts.note: a vessel that sank went under water
a perm is a permanent wave in hair

indicators.note: head means the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A wave strikes Bond's head while in a sunken craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hits' just links the wave to Bond's head, B.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository storing donated seed, a kind of store or container, for later conception.

clue.text: Bond in sight of gun — it explodes

indicators.note: in sight of means visible within, so the letters are seen among these words

explanation.surface: Bond stares down a gun as it goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To bond is to join together, a verb synonym.

clue.text: He gets a free lunch, old Bob taking credit: later to arrive, having no starter

indicators.note: taking says old Bob is followed by and takes on the credit abbreviation

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: born later means younger

explanation.surface: A freeloader, old Bob, runs up credit and turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is British slang for a shilling, whose old abbreviation was s.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger cadges things free from others, the type who never pays.
